text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Defence Minister Thage Peterson is moved closer to Prime Minister Goran Persson in a cabinet reshuffle to support the premier in the lead up to the September 1998 election. Trade Minister Bjorn von Sydow becomes the new Defence Minister and Leif Pagrotsky the new Trade Minister.

- Sweden is to investigate if Jewish money and Nazi gold entered the Swedish banking system during World War Two. Two working groups set up by the Foreign Affairs Ministry and the central bank will oversee the investigation while three people from outside the central bank try to establish over the next six months how much gold Sweden bought from Nazi Germany during the war.

- Sweden's central bank left its key interest rate, the repo, unchanged, despite the consumer price index showing an annualised disinflation trend for the third consecutive month -- the first time in 42 years. The CPI fell 0.2 percent in December.
- The latest figures for Swedish unemployment showed 401,288 people were out of work at the end of last year, a fall of 8,017 peopl
- Three cabinet ministers have moved around, making former Defence Mister Thage Peterson the right hand man of Prime Minister Goran Persson.

- Unemployment is forecast to rise further in Sweden in the spring before the changes through an expected government employment package kick in. The benefits not come through until the end of 1997, according to industry group Industriforbundet. The group forecst Gross Domestic Product rising 1.1 percnet in 1997 and 3.7 percent in 1998 and inflation at 1.2 percent in 1997 and betwen 3.0-3.5 percent in 1998.

- Prime Minister Goran Persson reorganises the Swedish cabinet. Trade Minister Bjorn von Sydow will replace Thage Peterson as Defence Minister whiel cabinet minister Leif Pagrotsky will step in as Trade Minister. Peterson, the former speaker of parliament, will be given a post elsewhere in the cabinet. The changes take effect February 1.

- Ten information technology firms made their debut on the Stockhom bourse last year while eight more companies announced intentions to list. On Tuesday it became clear that three -- Alfaskop Partners, Office and Entra -- would seek to list.

- Dairy company Arla and grocery chain ICA are the most valuable trademarks in Sweden, according to a survey by the Groth patent bureau and market research company Delfi. Coco-Cola came in 12th which company spokesman Claes Tellman said confirmed the potential in Sweden. The survey measured the trademark value of 139 firms.

- Svenska Handelsbanken forecast the economies of Nordic countries would grow by an average of over three percent this year. At the same time inflation will remain less than one percent in Sweden and 2.5 percent in Denmark. Senior economist in Copenhagen, Thomas Thygesen, feels both Finland and Sweden will stage a recovery in the next two to three years while 1997 will be a top year for Denmark.
